#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/profile-lib.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.7 (AC-2.9; PRD
# AC-9.1, AC-9.3; SDD D-9.1, D-9.3)
#
# .claude/data/profiles.yaml + .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh: precedence
# (explicit key > profile > fallback), every profile defines every key,
# `standard` equals the oracle captured before any reader changed
# (tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json), unknown profile, the
# mtime-keyed cache, the overrides line, the /loa Profile line, the readers
# that route through loa_knob, and the grep lint for direct reads.
# =============================================================================

bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    LIB="$R/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh"
    PROFILES="$R/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    ORACLE="$R/tests/fixtures/profiles/standard-oracle.json"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    CFG="$T/config.yaml"
    export LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE="$CFG"
    export LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE="$T/run/effective-config.json"
    : > "$CFG"
}

knob() { bash "$LIB" knob "$@"; }

@test "PL-1 every profile defines every key, and the key set is the nine optional keys" {
    run diff <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort) <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE" | sort)
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    for p in standard full; do
        run diff <(yq -r ".profiles.$p | keys | .[]" "$PROFILES" | sort) <(yq -r '.profiles.lean | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort)
        [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    done
    [ "$(yq -r '.profiles | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort | paste -sd, -)" = "full,lean,standard" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '.schema_version' "$PROFILES")" = "1" ]
    ! yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | grep -qx 'interview.pacing'
}

@test "PL-2 every profile value is a boolean; lean is all false and full all true" {
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles[][] | tag] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "!!bool" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.lean[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "false" ]
    [ "$(yq -r '[.profiles.full[]] | unique | .[]' "$PROFILES")" = "true" ]
}

@test "PL-3 standard equals the oracle captured before any reader changed" {
    local k want got
    while IFS= read -r k; do
        want=$(jq -r --arg k "$k" '.keys[$k].standard' "$ORACLE")
        got=$(yq -r ".profiles.standard[\"$k\"]" "$PROFILES")
        [ "$want" = "$got" ] || { echo "standard $k = $got, oracle $want"; return 1; }
    done < <(jq -r '.keys | keys[]' "$ORACLE")
    # Outside the two guardrail keys (whose default this cycle changes) the
    # oracle's standard IS the value the readers returned for the shipped example.
    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.") | not)
               | select(.value.standard != .value.example_today) | .key' "$ORACLE"
    [ -z "$output" ]
    run jq -r '.keys | to_entries[] | select(.key | startswith("guardrails.")) | "\(.value.example_today)/\(.value.standard)"' "$ORACLE"
    [ -z "$output" ]
}

@test "PL-5 precedence: explicit key beats the profile, the profile beats the fallback" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nknown_failures:\n  surface_at_session_start: true\nkarpathy_principles:\n  diff_lines_per_task: 250\n' > "$CFG"
    [ "$(knob known_failures.surface_at_session_start false)" = "true" ]     # explicit
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start true)" = "false" ]          # lean, not the fallback
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true)" = "false" ]   # lean
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100)" = "250" ]        # non-profile key, explicit
    [ "$(knob run_mode.stale_hours 7)" = "7" ]                               # non-profile key, fallback
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\n' > "$CFG"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start false)" = "true" ]
    : > "$CFG"
    [ "$(bash "$LIB" profile)" = "standard" ]
    [ "$(bash "$LIB" source)" = "default" ]
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning false)" = "true" ]   # standard, not the fallback
}

@test "PL-6 an explicit false is honoured (yq's // would read it as absent)" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\nguardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: false\n  danger_level:\n    enforce: false\n' > "$CFG"
    [ "$(knob guardrails.input.enabled true)" = "false" ]
    [ "$(knob guardrails.danger_level.enforce true)" = "false" ]
    [ "$(knob .guardrails.input.enabled true)" = "false" ]                   # leading dot accepted
}

@test "PL-7 an unknown profile warns once on stderr and resolves standard" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: turbo\n' > "$CFG"
    run --separate-stderr bash "$LIB" profile
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$output" = "standard" ]
    [[ "$stderr" == *'unknown loa.profile "turbo"; using standard'* ]]
    [ "$(bash "$LIB" source 2>/dev/null)" = "invalid" ]
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.require_success_criteria false 2>/dev/null)" = "true" ]
    # A non-string profile is unknown too.
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: [lean]\n' > "$CFG"
    [ "$(bash "$LIB" profile 2>/dev/null)" = "standard" ]
}

@test "PL-8 the cache is written once and rebuilt when the config or profiles.yaml changes" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\n' > "$CFG"
    touch -d '2026-01-01 00:00:00' "$CFG"
    knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x >/dev/null
    [ -f "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" = "lean" ]
    # Same stamps → served from the cache: a planted value proves the read path.
    jq '.knobs["decisions.surface_at_session_start"].value = "from-cache"' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" > "$T/c" && mv "$T/c" "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "from-cache" ]
    # A config edit with a new mtime rebuilds.
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\n' > "$CFG"
    touch -d '2026-01-02 00:00:00' "$CFG"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "true" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.profile' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" = "full" ]
    # A profiles.yaml edit rebuilds too.
    cp "$PROFILES" "$T/profiles.yaml"
    export LOA_PROFILES_FILE="$T/profiles.yaml"
    knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x >/dev/null
    yq -i '.profiles.full["decisions.surface_at_session_start"] = false' "$T/profiles.yaml"
    touch -d '2026-01-03 00:00:00' "$T/profiles.yaml"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "false" ]
}

@test "PL-9 a corrupt or foreign cache file is rebuilt, never trusted" {
    mkdir -p "$T/run"
    echo 'not json' > "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning x)" = "true" ]
    jq -e '.schema_version == 1' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" >/dev/null
    jq '.id = "other"' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" > "$T/c" && mv "$T/c" "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE"
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning x)" = "true" ]
    [ "$(jq -r '.id' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" != "other" ]
}

@test "PL-10 a seam config without a cache seam writes no cache (the repository cache is never touched)" {
    unset LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
    mkdir -p "$T/root/.claude/data"
    cp "$PROFILES" "$T/root/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    LOA_PROFILE_ROOT="$T/root" run bash "$LIB" knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x
    [ "$output" = "false" ]
    [ ! -e "$T/root/.run/effective-config.json" ]
}

@test "PL-11 overrides lists the explicit profile keys that differ from the profile, sorted" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\nguardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: true\ndecisions:\n  surface_at_session_start: false\nstructured_handoff:\n  enabled: true\n' > "$CFG"
    run bash "$LIB" overrides
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    [ "$output" = "$(printf 'guardrails.input.enabled=true\nstructured_handoff.enabled=true')" ]
}

@test "PL-12 a profiles.yaml key that names a floor key is ignored with a WARN" {
    cp "$PROFILES" "$T/profiles.yaml"
    yq -i '.profiles.standard["implement_gate.mode"] = "deny" | .profiles.standard["flatline_protocol"] = false' "$T/profiles.yaml"
    export LOA_PROFILES_FILE="$T/profiles.yaml"
    run --separate-stderr bash "$LIB" knob implement_gate.mode ask
    [ "$output" = "ask" ]
    [[ "$stderr" == *"profiles.yaml key implement_gate.mode names a floor key; ignored"* ]]
    [[ "$stderr" == *"profiles.yaml key flatline_protocol names a floor key; ignored"* ]]
    [ "$(jq -r '.profile_keys | index("implement_gate.mode")' "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE")" = "null" ]
}

    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start true)" = "false" ]          # lean, not the fallback
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning true)" = "false" ]   # lean
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.diff_lines_per_task 100)" = "250" ]        # non-profile key, explicit
    [ "$(knob run_mode.stale_hours 7)" = "7" ]                               # non-profile key, fallback
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\n' > "$CFG"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start false)" = "true" ]
    : > "$CFG"
    [ "$(bash "$LIB" profile)" = "standard" ]
    [ "$(bash "$LIB" source)" = "default" ]
    [ "$(knob karpathy_principles.surgical_diff_warning false)" = "true" ]   # standard, not the fallback
}

@test "PL-6 an explicit false is honoured (yq's // would read it as absent)" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: full\nguardrails:\n  input:\n    enabled: false\n  danger_level:\n    enforce: false\n' > "$CFG"
    [ "$(knob guardrails.input.enabled true)" = "false" ]
    [ "$(knob guardrails.danger_level.enforce true)" = "false" ]

}

@test "PL-7 an unknown profile warns once on stderr and resolves standard" {

    [ "$output" = "standard" ]

    [ "$(bash "$LIB" profile 2>/dev/null)" = "standard" ]
}

@test "PL-8 the cache is written once and rebuilt when the config or profiles.yaml changes" {
    printf 'loa:\n  profile: lean\n' > "$CFG"

    knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x >/dev/null
    [ -f "$LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE" ]

    yq -i '.profiles.full["decisions.surface_at_session_start"] = false' "$T/profiles.yaml"
    touch -d '2026-01-03 00:00:00' "$T/profiles.yaml"
    [ "$(knob decisions.surface_at_session_start x)" = "false" ]
}

}

== implement-gate
1..33
not ok 1 IG-1 a lead-session payload carrying tool_input.active_skill records active_skill_seen_at and its source
not ok 2 IG-2 the recorder writes once: an existing active_skill_seen_at is kept, other keys are preserved, no temp file is left
not ok 3 IG-3 a teammate role or a subagent payload writes nothing
not ok 4 IG-4 the corpus' records_evidence column holds for every fixture
not ok 5 IG-5 a forged active_skill Write payload does not flip the gate, whatever .run/ claims
not ok 6 IG-6 without the opt-in the gate stays heuristic: every corpus fixture gets its heuristic decision
not ok 7 IG-7 with implement_gate.mode: authoritative the branch passes the payload corpus
not ok 8 IG-8 the authoritative branch falls back to the heuristic on a payload without active_skill (RUNNING allows, absent asks)
not ok 9 IG-9 detect-platform-features.sh: the env var and the probe file no longer set the flag; the evidence is reported, never promoted
not ok 10 IG-10 the /loa evidence line: mode and evidence, read-only
not ok 11 IG-12 authoritative is strictly tighter than heuristic: with RUNNING state a non-implementation claim asks and logs one ask row, each implementation claim one heuristic row
== run-checkpoint-derive
1..22
not ok 1 RCD-1 drift fixture (D-5.4): cache RUNNING, three COMPLETED markers with APPROVED trailers, ledger completed → COMPLETE; --write makes the cache say so
not ok 2 RCD-2 a stale marker whose trailers name sprint-1 of another cycle (or whose sprint: line names another sprint) is stale_marker, not counted
not ok 3 RCD-3 legacy feedback (no LOA-VERDICT trailer) yields no verdict: the sprint stays incomplete and the file is named in derivation.legacy_feedback
not ok 4 RCD-4 review and audit APPROVED without a marker is awaiting_marker (counted incomplete); a marker with the ledger row not completed is in_progress
not ok 5 RCD-5 JACKED_OUT is terminal: a cache .state or .status JACKED_OUT, or .completion.merged_sha, stays JACKED_OUT with contradicting files reported as drift
not ok 6 RCD-6 HALTED is sticky: a cache HALTED stays HALTED even when every sprint is complete; a breaker OPEN halts a RUNNING cache
not ok 7 RCD-7 COMPLETE never moves back to RUNNING unless the ledger registers a new incomplete sprint
not ok 8 RCD-8 an incomplete sprint is RUNNING while last_activity is within run_mode.stale_hours (default 12), else INTERRUPTED; the key widens the window
not ok 9 RCD-9 breaker recompute: two -r1 feedback files and a zeroed breaker give cycle_count 2, same_issue 2, no_progress 1; counters are raised, never lowered
not ok 10 RCD-10 three identical changes-required rounds meet the same-issue threshold: the derived breaker trips OPEN (history source derive) and the run derives HALTED
not ok 11 RCD-11 schema tolerance: a file without derived_at, derivation or .status reads fine, gains the fields on --write and keeps its schema_version

All subsequent `.run/*.json` mutations in this skill MUST use the atomic write pattern: pipe the
`jq` transform to a `.tmp` sibling, then `mv` the `.tmp` file over the original — never edit the
JSON file in place.

## Main Loop — Single Sprint (`/run sprint-N`)

```
while circuit_breaker.state == CLOSED:
  1. /implement $target
  2. Commit changes, then track deletions (see "Deleted Files Tracking" below)
  3. update_state(phase: REVIEW); checkpoint(phase: REVIEW)
  4. /review-sprint $target
  5. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate review` on engineer-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` (anything else — including an inconsistent trailer — counts as
     findings) → record-round (see "Circuit Breaker" below); exit 10, HALT; else continue
     loop (back to step 1)
  6. update_state(phase: AUDIT); checkpoint(phase: AUDIT)
  7. /audit-sprint $target
  8. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate audit` on auditor-sprint-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` → same as step 5 (golden-path's `_gp_sprint_is_audited` additionally
     re-derives the review trailer and cross-checks `excluded` ⇔ `excluded_confirmed`)
  9. RED_TEAM_CODE gate (if enabled) — see resources/conditional-procedures.md §red-team-code-gate
  10. If COMPLETED marker exists → update_state(state: COMPLETE); break
Create draft PR (see "Completion and PR Creation" — resources/completion-modes.md)
Invoke Post-PR Validation if enabled — resources/conditional-procedures.md §post-pr-validation
Update state to READY_FOR_HITL or JACKED_OUT
```

Call `check_rate_limit` (see "Rate Limiting" below) before each of steps 1, 4, and 7.
`checkpoint(...)` = `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint $target --phase <PHASE>`
(when `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` exists); `/implement` writes the per-task checkpoint on each
`br close`. Beads stay the recovery truth — the checkpoint is a hint `/run-resume` reports.

## Circuit Breaker

After each `/review-sprint` and `/audit-sprint`, run
`.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file <feedback-file> --sprint $target`.
It updates `.run/circuit-breaker.json` (same-issue hash, no-progress, cycle count, timeout; thresholds in that
file and `run_mode.defaults`); exit 10 has already written `OPEN` and `HALTED` — report its
`TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` line, then "Run halted. Use `/run-resume --reset-ice` to continue."

§red-team-code-gate for behavior).

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/karpathy-surgical-diff.bats — cycle-129 sprint-256 Task 2.3
# (AC-2.3; PRD AC-4.3; SDD D-4.3, D-4.2a; DEC-0141)
#
# The surgical-diff hook keys its running total on the checkpoint task
# (`run-checkpoint.sh read --json`), else the sprint, else the session id;
# keeps one sanitised file per task under the state directory (at most 20);
# deletes the legacy session-long file; writes the summary the review's
# SURGICAL axis reads; and is silent when the knob is off. A fixture
# checkpoint (LOA_RUN_DIR) and a fake `br` on PATH stand in for a live run.
# =============================================================================

bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

setup() {
    R="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    HOOK="$R/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh"
    command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not available"
    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not available"
    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
    export LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$T/config.yaml"
    export KARPATHY_STATE_DIR="$T/state"
    export KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE="$T/summary.json"
    export KARPATHY_LEGACY_STATE="$T/karpathy-task-state.jsonl"
    export KARPATHY_TRAJECTORY_DIR="$T/trajectory"
    export LOA_RUN_DIR="$T/run"
    unset LOA_SESSION_ID LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE LOA_PROFILE_CACHE_FILE
    mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/bin"
    printf 'karpathy_principles:\n  surgical_diff_warning: true\n  diff_lines_per_task: 5\n' > "$LOA_CONFIG_OVERRIDE"
    # Fake beads: every bead reports closed unless BR_STATUS says otherwise.
    printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'printf "{\"status\":\"%s\"}\n" "${BR_STATUS:-closed}"' > "$T/bin/br"
    chmod +x "$T/bin/br"
    export PATH="$T/bin:$PATH"
}

# checkpoint <sprint> [task] — a schema-2 run state with that checkpoint
checkpoint() {
    jq -n --arg s "$1" --arg t "${2:-}" \
        '{schema_version: 2, state: "RUNNING",
          checkpoint: {sprint: $s, task: (if $t == "" then null else $t end), phase: "IMPLEMENT", ts: "2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"}}' \
        > "$T/run/sprint-plan-state.json"
}

# write_lines <n> [session_id] — one Write payload adding n lines
write_lines() {
    local n="$1" sid="${2:-sess-1}" content
    content=$(seq 1 "$n" | paste -sd'\n' -)
    jq -nc --arg c "$content" --arg s "$sid" \
        '{tool_name: "Write", session_id: $s, tool_input: {file_path: "/repo/src/x.sh", content: $c}}' \
        | bash "$HOOK"
}

    [ "$(jq -r '.lines' "$KARPATHY_SUMMARY_FILE")" = "5" ]

## Phase -2: Beads-First Integration

### Task Tracking: Beads vs TaskCreate

Use `br` (beads_rust) exclusively for sprint task lifecycle (commands below). Claude's `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` are for session-level progress display only; tasks tracked only there are invisible to cross-session recovery, `/run-resume`, and beads health checks.

```bash
health=$(.claude/scripts/beads/beads-health.sh --quick --json)
status=$(echo "$health" | jq -r '.status')
```

`HEALTHY` → import state (`br sync --import-only`; `update-beads-state.sh --sync-import`) and proceed. `DEGRADED` → warn, import, proceed. `NOT_INSTALLED`/`NOT_INITIALIZED` → check opt-out (`update-beads-state.sh --opt-out-check`); without one, warn (`cargo install beads_rust && br init` to add it) and fall back to markdown. `MIGRATION_NEEDED`/`UNHEALTHY` → warn, fall back to markdown. Record the outcome: `.claude/scripts/beads/update-beads-state.sh --health "$status"`.

Run the full lifecycle per task yourself: health check → `br sync --import-only` → `.claude/scripts/beads/get-ready-work.sh` (not bare `br ready`) → `br update <id> --status in_progress` → implement → `br close <id>` (run mode: then `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint sprint-N --task <id> --phase IMPLEMENT`) → `br sync --flush-only` at session end. Log discovered issues as they surface — this adds a `discovered-during:<parent-id>` label for traceability:

```bash
.claude/scripts/beads/log-discovered-issue.sh "$CURRENT_TASK_ID" "Description of discovered issue" bug 2

+
+# =========================================================================
+# cycle-129 D-4.2 (AC-2.2): a pure-review skill (role: review,
+# capabilities.write_files: false) strips Write, Edit and NotebookEdit
+# =========================================================================
+
+# pure_review_skill <name> [disallowed-tools block lines...]
+pure_review_skill() {
+    local name="$1"; shift
+    local dis=""
+    [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && dis="$(printf '%s\n' "$@")"
+    create_skill "$name" "---
+name: $name
+description: pure review fixture
+role: review
+allowed-tools: Read, Grep, Glob
+${dis}
+capabilities:
+  schema_version: 1
+  read_files: true
+  search_code: true
+  write_files: false
+  execute_commands: false
+  web_access: false
+  user_interaction: false
+  agent_spawn: false
+  task_management: false
+cost-profile: lightweight
+---
+# Pure review: review and verify findings"
+}
+
+@test "c129-D4.2: a pure-review skill without disallowed-tools fails by name" {
+    pure_review_skill bare-review
+    SKILLS_DIR="$FIXTURE_DIR" run "$VALIDATOR" --skill bare-review
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"pure-review skill (role: review, capabilities.write_files: false) must carry disallowed-tools: Write, Edit, NotebookEdit — missing: Write, Edit, NotebookEdit"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "c129-D4.2: a pure-review skill missing one of the three fails naming it" {
+    pure_review_skill partial-review "disallowed-tools:" "  - Write" "  - Edit"

head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:327 — `resolve` treats only JACKED_OUT, HALTED and COMPLETE as sticky. head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:78 — The BSD fallback `stat -Lf '%N|%Fm|%z'` also runs on GNU systems whenever the GNU `stat -Lc` exits non-zero, which happens as soon as any of the three inputs is missing (a missing floor.yaml or profiles.yaml is handled as a supported state elsewhere in this file). Reproduced: with floor.yaml absent, switching the config from `profile: lean` to `profile: full` still returns lean values from `.run/effective-config.json`. Keep one fixture that is expected to exit exactly 0 (stub the environment-dependent checks) instead of loosening the assertion.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
The review is in `/workspace/review.md`: 11 findings and **Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED**. I reproduced the first three by running copies of the scripts under `/tmp`; nothing under `pr/` was changed.

**Main defects:**
1. **The run-position step breaks on jq 1.6** (`run-checkpoint.sh:378`). The script uses the jq variable name `$label`, which jq 1.6 rejects as a keyword. jq 1.6 is the default on Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04, and it is what this machine has. Every derive then exits 3, so no derived run position is ever written. The implement gate's deny mode then always treats the position as unknown, and `/loa` drops its Run line without any message.
2. **A run waiting for human review comes back to life** (`run-checkpoint.sh:327`). A cache in the READY_FOR_HITL state with recent activity gets rewritten to RUNNING. The implement gate then accepts that as an active run and allows writes.
3. **The profile cache can serve stale values** (`profile-lib.sh:78`). If any input file is missing, the GNU `stat` call fails and the BSD fallback runs. On Linux that fallback reports file-system statistics instead of file times and sizes. With `floor.yaml` absent, switching the config from `lean` to `full` still returned the `lean` values.
4. **Copying the example config makes the profile setting do nothing** (`.loa.config.yaml.example:33`). The example sets 8 of the 9 profile keys explicitly, and an explicit key always wins. `lean` and `full` then change only `soul_identity_doc.enabled`.
5. **The surgical-diff counter credits the wrong task** (`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:132`). It keys on `.checkpoint.task`, which by the repo's own schema is the last *closed* bead. Each task's lines land in the previous task's file, so the reviewer's per-bead SURGICAL check is off by one task.

**Lower-severity findings:**
- **Stale warning text:** the surgical-diff warning still says "Session diff total", though the count is now per task.
- **Marker expiry:** the 2-hour marker is never refreshed. Under deny mode, a direct `/implement` session longer than that has its own writes refused instead of asked about.
- **Stale cache masks a live run:** an old `sprint-plan-state.json` makes the gate skip the `state.json` and simstim checks, so a live `/run sprint-N` loses its sanction.
- **Env-var overrides work in production:** the profile library's override variables (`LOA_PROFILE_CONFIG_FILE` and others) have no test-only gate. One variable can redirect the guardrail and danger-level switches.
- **The cache can be forged:** the cache in `.run/` is writable from Bash and its key is easy to recompute, so a fake cache can override an explicit guardrail setting.
- **Weaker lint self-test:** the "exit 0" assertion now also accepts exit 1, so new warnings on a clean tree would go unnoticed.

**What I checked and the limits:** the fence corpus passes in full (89/89 benign allowed, 142/142 dangerous blocked), and further probes found no bypass in the new heredoc classifier. Most bats suites failed here, but only because `pr/` holds just the touched files and they depend on the rest of the repo, so those results don't reflect the change. Two karpathy test files also fail to parse because of a `REDACTED-TEST-SECRET` line. The same line is already in the base version, so I treated it as an artifact of how the PR was frozen, not as a defect.
